NVDA.t: The main event of earnings season: Street expects $2.08 EPS on ~$91.9B revenue, which would be ~85% growth from a year ago. Reports after the close Aug 26; AI data-center demand and guidance will drive the reaction more than the headline numbers.

WMT.t: Walmart reports Aug 20 with $0.74 EPS expected on ~$186.7B revenue (~7% yoy). Watch e-commerce growth and any read on consumer spending health heading into the holidays.

GFI.t: Gold Fields reports Aug 25 with $2.63 EPS expected on $5.8B revenue. Revenue is running ~137% above last year on higher gold prices and production — cost control is the swing factor.

RY.t: Royal Bank of Canada reports Aug 27, $2.89 EPS expected on $12.9B revenue. Credit-loss provisions and margin trends are the usual swing factors for the Canadian banks.

HD.t: Home Depot kicks off big-box retail week Aug 18: $4.73 EPS expected on $47.3B revenue (~5% yoy). Comparable sales and big-ticket demand are the numbers to watch.

BABA.t: Alibaba reports its June quarter Aug 20 with $1.50 EPS expected on $39.5B revenue. Cloud growth and AI spending commentary tend to move the stock more than the topline.

BHP.t: BHP reports Aug 17 with $2.67 EPS expected on ~$30.2B revenue. Iron ore and copper pricing drive results; watch the dividend declaration.

TD.t: TD Bank reports Aug 27, $1.73 EPS expected on $10.8B revenue, with revenue tracking ~5% below last year. US business performance remains the focus.

TCOM.t: Trip.com reports Aug 26 with $0.88 EPS expected on $2.3B revenue (~17% yoy). Outbound Chinese travel recovery is the growth engine to watch.

CRWD.t: CrowdStrike reports Aug 26: $0.29 EPS expected on $1.44B revenue, ~26% yoy growth. ARR growth and net-new customer adds are the metrics that move this one.

MRVL.t: Marvell reports Aug 27 with $0.93 EPS expected on $2.7B revenue (~28% yoy). Custom AI silicon ramp is the story — data-center segment growth is the number to watch.

ADI.t: Analog Devices reports Aug 19: $3.34 EPS expected on $3.9B revenue, ~37% yoy. Industrial and auto chip demand recovery is the key theme.

BMO.t: Bank of Montreal reports Aug 25 with $2.67 EPS expected on $6.9B revenue. Flat yoy revenue puts the focus on credit quality and expense control.

TJX.t: TJX reports Aug 19: $1.19 EPS expected on $15.2B revenue (~9% yoy). The off-price model has been a consistent share-gainer — comp sales guidance is key.

HMY.t: Harmony Gold reports Aug 27 with $1.29 EPS expected on $3.2B revenue — running ~56% above last year on gold strength.

DE.t: Deere reports Aug 20: $4.71 EPS expected on $10.8B revenue. Ag equipment demand and 2027 order book commentary set the tone.

CRM.t: Salesforce reports Aug 26 with $3.27 EPS expected on $11.3B revenue (~13% yoy). AI product monetization (Agentforce) and margin trajectory are the focus.

CM.t: CIBC reports Aug 27, $1.78 EPS expected on $5.7B revenue. Like the other Canadian banks, provisions and margins matter most.

BNS.t: Scotiabank reports Aug 25 with $1.48 EPS expected on $7.1B revenue, tracking ~4% below last year. International banking performance is the swing factor.

BEKE.t: KE Holdings reports Aug 21: $0.31 EPS expected on $3.6B revenue, down ~19% yoy amid China property softness. Transaction volume trends are the tell.

ZTO.t: ZTO Express reports Aug 18 after the close: $0.50 EPS expected on $2.2B revenue (~22% yoy). Parcel volume growth vs. price competition is the balance to watch.

PDD.t: PDD reports Aug 24 with $2.73 EPS expected on $17B revenue (~10% yoy). Temu economics and domestic competition commentary drive sentiment.

LOW.t: Lowe's reports Aug 19 before the open: $4.23 EPS expected on $26.2B revenue (~10% yoy). Comps vs. Home Depot's print a day earlier will be the comparison.

LI.t: Li Auto reports Aug 26, expected around breakeven (-$0.01 EPS) on $3.9B revenue, down ~12% yoy in a brutal China EV price war. Delivery guidance matters most.

HTHT.t: H World Group reports Aug 17: $0.74 EPS expected on ~$1.0B revenue (~11% yoy). RevPAR trends in China hotels are the key metric.

INTU.t: Intuit closes its fiscal year Aug 25 after the close: $3.54 EPS expected on $4.3B revenue (~10% yoy). FY2027 guidance and AI feature monetization are the focus.

NTES.t: NetEase reports Aug 20 with $2.30 EPS expected on $4.3B revenue (~12% yoy). New game pipeline performance drives the quarter.

ROST.t: Ross Stores reports Aug 19: $1.94 EPS expected on $6.2B revenue (~21% yoy). Off-price continues to take share — watch comp guidance.

SNPS.t: Synopsys reports Aug 26 with $3.67 EPS expected on $2.4B revenue — ~42% yoy including the Ansys acquisition. Integration progress and AI design demand are key.

TGT.t: Target reports Aug 19: $2.26 EPS expected on $26.1B revenue (~7% yoy). Traffic trends and discretionary category recovery are the watch items.

WDS.t: Woodside Energy reports Aug 25 with $0.78 EPS expected on $3.6B revenue, roughly flat yoy. Production guidance and LNG pricing drive the result.

KEYS.t: Keysight reports Aug 18: $2.48 EPS expected on $1.75B revenue. Order trends in electronic test — especially AI/data-center related — are the focus.

ADSK.t: Autodesk reports Aug 27 with $3.12 EPS expected on ~$2.0B revenue (~18% yoy). Billings growth and margin progress are the metrics that matter.

VIK.t: Viking Holdings reports Aug 19: $1.26 EPS expected on $2.1B revenue (~18% yoy). Booking curve and 2027 pricing commentary are key for cruise demand.

HEI.t: HEICO reports Aug 25 with $1.51 EPS expected on $1.35B revenue (~25% yoy). Aerospace aftermarket demand has been the consistent growth driver.

A.t: Agilent reports Aug 26: $1.49 EPS expected on $1.8B revenue (~10% yoy). Lab instrument demand recovery, especially in China, is the theme.

WDAY.t: Workday reports Aug 27 with $2.61 EPS expected on $2.6B revenue (~14% yoy). Subscription revenue guidance and AI product traction are the focus.

BIDU.t: Baidu reports Aug 18: $1.51 EPS expected on $4.7B revenue (~4% yoy). AI cloud growth vs. ad softness is the tension in the story.

HAFN.t: Hafnia reports Aug 28 with $0.56 EPS expected on ~$0.4B revenue. Product tanker rates (~23% yoy revenue growth) drive the result.

VEEV.t: Veeva reports Aug 26: $2.22 EPS expected on $0.9B revenue (~16% yoy). Life-sciences software demand has held up well; watch billings guidance.

UI.t: Ubiquiti reports Aug 21 with $4.03 EPS expected on $0.85B revenue (~19% yoy). Enterprise networking demand and channel inventory are the variables.

EL.t: Estee Lauder reports Aug 19 before the open: $0.32 EPS expected on $3.6B revenue. The turnaround story hinges on China and travel-retail recovery.

BWLP.t: BW LPG reports Aug 28: $1.25 EPS expected on $0.33B revenue, down ~7% yoy on softer VLGC rates.

MNSO.t: Miniso reports Aug 28 with $0.28 EPS expected on $0.85B revenue (~34% yoy). Store expansion pace and IP-product mix drive the growth story.

DG.t: Dollar General reports Aug 27: $2.01 EPS expected on $11.2B revenue (~3% yoy). Core customer health and shrink improvement are the key themes.

P.t: Reports Aug 26 with $0.58 EPS expected on $1.1B revenue, ~35% yoy growth — one of the stronger growth profiles reporting that day.

WSM.t: Williams-Sonoma reports Aug 25 before the open: $2.07 EPS expected on $1.9B revenue (~4% yoy). Margin resilience has been the standout — watch furniture demand.

ZM.t: Zoom reports Aug 25 with $1.48 EPS expected on $1.3B revenue (~6% yoy). Enterprise growth and AI Companion adoption are the needle-movers.

AFRM.t: Affirm reports Aug 27: $0.35 EPS expected on $1.1B revenue. GMV growth and credit performance are the two numbers that drive this stock.

HPQ.t: HP reports Aug 26 with $0.66 EPS expected on $14.4B revenue (~9% yoy). PC refresh cycle strength and print margins are the watch items.

OKTA.t: Okta reports Aug 26: $0.97 EPS expected on $0.79B revenue (~11% yoy). Net revenue retention and new product attach (identity governance) matter most.

DLTR.t: Dollar Tree reports Aug 27 with $1.12 EPS expected on $4.9B revenue (~7% yoy). Multi-price rollout progress is the story.

BURL.t: Burlington reports Aug 26: $2.18 EPS expected on $3.0B revenue (~14% yoy). Off-price momentum and margin expansion are the focus.

ULTA.t: Ulta reports Aug 26 with $6.17 EPS expected on $3.0B revenue (~11% yoy). Comp growth and competitive dynamics in beauty are the key questions.

AS.t: Amer Sports reports Aug 18: $0.11 EPS expected on $1.5B revenue (~32% yoy). Arc'teryx growth in China remains the headline driver.

CDLR.t: Cadeler reports Aug 25 with $0.98 EPS expected on $0.28B revenue — roughly doubling yoy as offshore wind installation vessels come online.

SQM.t: SQM reports Aug 19: $2.03 EPS expected on $2.2B revenue (~70% yoy on lithium recovery). Lithium pricing commentary is the market-mover.

TRMD.t: TORM reports Aug 26 with $3.35 EPS expected on $0.51B revenue (~20% yoy). Product tanker rates drive everything here.

FN.t: Fabrinet reports Aug 17: $3.81 EPS expected on $1.3B revenue (~39% yoy). Optical component demand from AI data centers is the growth engine.

DKS.t: Dick's Sporting Goods reports Aug 24 with $3.78 EPS expected on $5.7B revenue. Watch integration commentary on the Foot Locker acquisition.

BBY.t: Best Buy reports Aug 27: $1.37 EPS expected on $9.6B revenue (~2% yoy). AI-PC upgrade cycle and appliance demand are the swing factors.

RBRK.t: Rubrik reports Aug 27, expected around breakeven ($0.04 EPS) on $0.40B revenue (~39% yoy). Subscription ARR growth is the metric that matters.

NDSN.t: Nordson reports Aug 19 with $3.09 EPS expected on $0.78B revenue (~9% yoy). Electronics dispensing demand is the cyclical driver.

CSCO.t: Cisco's report landed mixed: EPS of $0.98 came in below the $1.17 consensus while revenue of $17.3B beat by ~2.5% (12% yoy growth). AI infrastructure orders remain the bright spot investors are tracking.

AMAT.t: Applied Materials reported EPS of $3.20 vs $3.40 expected, a ~6% miss, though revenue of $9.1B edged past estimates (11% yoy growth). Semi-cap equipment guidance drove the post-print reaction.

UNH.t: UnitedHealth delivered a big beat: EPS of $6.05 vs $4.94 expected (+22%) on $112B revenue. Medical cost trends remain the number the market scrutinizes most.

WDC.t: Western Digital posted EPS well ahead of the $3.31 estimate on revenue of $3.75B, slightly above consensus and up ~28% yoy on strong storage demand.

SE.t: Sea Limited matched EPS estimates ($0.86) and beat on revenue: $7.8B vs $7.1B expected, up ~47% yoy. E-commerce and fintech both contributed to the topline strength.

SPG.t: Simon Property missed on FFO-adjusted EPS ($1.49 vs $1.64, -9%) but beat slightly on revenue at $1.66B (+19% yoy). Occupancy and leasing spreads remain healthy.

NU.t: Nu Holdings beat on both lines: EPS of $0.22 (+11% vs estimates) on $5.9B revenue (+9% vs estimates, ~53% yoy). Customer growth in Brazil and Mexico continues to compound.

NBIS.t: Nebius posted a much smaller loss than expected (-$0.12 vs -$0.72 est) on in-line revenue of $0.58B. AI infrastructure buildout remains the story.

LITE.t: Lumentum beat on both lines: EPS $3.23 vs $2.97 expected (+9%) on $1.0B revenue, up ~90% yoy on AI optical demand.

COHR.t: Coherent beat estimates with EPS of $1.74 vs $1.62 (+7%) on $2.05B revenue (+3% vs est, ~21% yoy). AI transceiver demand keeps driving the growth.

CRWV.t: CoreWeave's loss of $1.03/share was narrower than the $1.21 expected, with revenue of $2.6B slightly ahead and up ~112% yoy. Capacity expansion pace is the key debate.

CBRS.t: Reported a much smaller loss than expected (-$0.04 vs -$0.17 est) with revenue of $0.21B beating estimates by ~10%.

CAH.t: Cardinal Health beat big on EPS: $2.91 vs $2.42 expected (+20%), though revenue of $63.7B came in ~2% light. Specialty distribution strength drove the bottom line.

FERG.t: Ferguson beat modestly on both lines: EPS $3.39 (+3%) on $8.75B revenue (+9% yoy). Non-residential construction demand held up well.

RKLB.t: Rocket Lab's loss of $0.08/share was wider than the $0.06 expected on in-line revenue of $0.23B (+64% yoy). Neutron development timeline remains the focus.

FNV.t: Franco-Nevada missed on both lines: EPS $1.81 vs $1.95 (-7%) on revenue of $0.58B (-6% vs est), though revenue still grew ~77% yoy on gold strength.

CIG.t: CEMIG matched EPS estimates on revenue of $1.84B, slightly ahead of consensus and up ~19% yoy.

ALC.t: Alcon beat nicely: EPS $0.84 vs $0.77 (+9%) on $2.8B revenue (+3% vs est, ~7% yoy). Surgical equipment demand led the quarter.

BAP.t: Credicorp was essentially in line on EPS ($7.29 vs $7.31) with revenue of $1.9B beating by ~5% (+17% yoy).

VG.t: Venture Global beat on EPS ($0.51 vs $0.48) though revenue of $4.6B was ~2% light — still up ~59% yoy on LNG capacity ramp.

TPR.t: Tapestry beat: EPS $1.32 vs $1.28 on $1.88B revenue, up ~21% yoy. Coach brand momentum continues to carry the story.

ASTS.t: AST SpaceMobile's loss was wider than expected (-$0.44 vs -$0.32 est). Pre-revenue satellite buildout continues; launch cadence is the catalyst.

BSP.t: Crushed EPS estimates ($0.46 vs $0.24 expected, +89%) on in-line revenue of $0.70B.

SMCI.t: Super Micro beat EPS estimates by a wide margin ($1.70 vs $0.92) though revenue of $11.1B was ~4% light — still up ~123% yoy on AI server demand.

IHG.t: IHG beat on EPS ($2.75 vs $2.65) with revenue slightly light at $2.66B, up ~37% yoy. RevPAR growth and buybacks remain the capital-return story.

AMCR.t: Amcor beat on both lines: EPS $1.23 (+3%) on $6.4B revenue (+6% vs est, ~77% yoy including the Berry merger).

PAAS.t: Pan American Silver missed on EPS ($0.73 vs $0.84, -13%) with revenue of $1.1B slightly light — still up ~49% yoy on metal prices.

ONON.t: On Holding beat on EPS ($0.44 vs $0.42) though revenue of $1.05B came in ~3% below estimates. DTC growth and full-year guidance are the focus.

KSPI.t: Kaspi.kz was in line: EPS $2.85 vs $2.87 expected on matching revenue of $2.3B, up ~32% yoy.

QNT.t: Reported a slightly wider loss than expected (-$0.28 vs -$0.26 est) with revenue modestly ahead of the small base analysts modeled.

PFGC.t: Performance Food Group was essentially in line: EPS $1.59 vs $1.60 on $18.0B revenue (+6% yoy).

ESLT.t: Elbit Systems was in line on EPS ($3.71 vs $3.69) with revenue of $2.3B slightly ahead, up ~16% yoy on defense demand.

PS.t: Beat on EPS ($0.14 vs $0.13 expected) though revenue came in ~9% below estimates.
